nature.name: Flamingo City in the Great Rann
nature.what: Tens of thousands of greater and lesser flamingos gather to nest and feed in the shallow salt flats of Kutch, one of the largest flamingo colonies in Asia.
nature.tip: The nesting ground itself is restricted; go with a local guide from Bhuj and watch from the edges of the Rann at dawn.

nature.name: Lesser flamingos of Thane Creek
nature.what: Mumbai's own pink tide: thousands of lesser flamingos feed on the mudflats of Thane Creek, within sight of the city's towers.
nature.tip: Take a boat ride from the Coastal and Marine Biodiversity Centre at Airoli. Time it with high tide, when the birds come closest.

nature.name: Winter at Keoladeo, Bharatpur
nature.what: Over 350 species have been recorded at this UNESCO wetland; in winter it fills with ducks, geese, painted storks and raptors from Central Asia and Siberia.
nature.tip: Hire a cycle rickshaw with a naturalist puller at the gate and start at opening time, when the birds are most active.

nature.name: Demoiselle cranes of Khichan
nature.what: Thousands of demoiselle cranes fly in from Central Asia and land in this desert village every morning to be fed grain by the villagers, a tradition going back generations.
nature.tip: Be at the feeding ground (chugga ghar) by 7 am. Watch quietly from the rooftops; don't walk into the enclosure.

nature.name: Amur falcons of Pangti
nature.what: Up to a million Amur falcons roost around the Doyang reservoir on their journey from Siberia to Africa. Once hunted here, they are now protected by the community.
nature.tip: Dusk and dawn, when clouds of falcons wheel over the roost, are the moments. Stay in Wokha or a Pangti homestay.

nature.name: Olive ridley turtles nesting
nature.what: In an arribada, tens of thousands of olive ridley turtles come ashore together on a few nights to lay eggs, one of the great wildlife spectacles anywhere. Hatchlings follow about 45 days later.
nature.tip: Rushikulya beach near Ganjam is the most accessible site. Dates vary each year; check with the forest department and never use flash or torches.

nature.name: Chilika's winter birds
nature.what: Asia's largest brackish-water lagoon hosts lakhs of migratory birds each winter; Mangalajodi, run by former poachers turned guides, gets you closest.
nature.tip: Go out on a boat at Mangalajodi at sunrise. At Satapada, the same trip can bring Irrawaddy dolphins.

nature.name: Kaas Plateau in bloom
nature.what: For a few weeks after the monsoon this UNESCO-listed plateau turns into carpets of pink, purple and yellow wildflowers, including many found nowhere else.
nature.tip: Entry is limited and slots are booked online. Go on a weekday, early, and stay on the paths.

nature.name: Valley of Flowers
nature.what: A high glacial valley carpeted with hundreds of species of alpine flowers through the monsoon, part of the Nanda Devi UNESCO site.
nature.tip: The trek starts from Govindghat via Ghangaria; the valley is a day visit only. Combine it with Hemkund Sahib.

nature.name: Neelakurinji, the 12-year bloom
nature.what: The hills around Munnar turn blue when Strobilanthes kunthiana flowers en masse, once every twelve years. The last great bloom was in 2018.
nature.tip: Smaller patches flower in other years across the Nilgiris and Kodaikanal. Watch local news from August.

nature.name: Fireflies of Bhandardara
nature.what: Just before the monsoon, trees around Bhandardara and Purushwadi light up with millions of synchronised fireflies, flashing together like fairy lights.
nature.tip: Stay overnight in a village homestay. Keep torches and phones dark, and don't catch them.

nature.name: Rhododendrons of Sikkim
nature.what: Sikkim has around 40 species of rhododendron, and in spring whole hillsides at Barsey and Yumthang flush red, pink and white.
nature.tip: Barsey sanctuary is an easy walk from Hilley. Yumthang needs a permit arranged through a Gangtok tour operator.

nature.name: Cherry blossom in Shillong
nature.what: Himalayan wild cherry trees bloom pink across Shillong in late autumn, unusually for cherries, and the city celebrates with a festival.
nature.tip: Ward's Lake, Upper Shillong and the roads near the Polo Ground are the prettiest spots.

nature.name: Tulip Garden, Srinagar
nature.what: Asia's largest tulip garden, on the slopes of the Zabarwan hills above Dal Lake, flowers with over a million tulips for about three weeks.
nature.tip: Open only for about a month. Go at opening time to see the rows before the crowds.

nature.name: Saffron harvest, Pampore
nature.what: For about two weeks the karewa fields of Pampore turn violet with crocus flowers, picked by hand at dawn for their red stigmas.
nature.tip: Visit in the early morning when families are harvesting, and buy saffron directly from growers.

nature.name: Monsoon in Sohra (Cherrapunji)
nature.what: Among the wettest places on earth: clouds pour through the valleys, waterfalls appear on every cliff and the living root bridges glisten.
nature.tip: Carry proper rain gear and good shoes. Views come and go in minutes, so sit tight when the cloud rolls in.

nature.name: Snow leopard season
nature.what: In deep winter, snow leopards follow ibex and blue sheep down to lower slopes around Kibber in Spiti and Rumbak in Ladakh's Hemis park.
nature.tip: Go with a local spotting team and homestay; temperatures drop below −20°C. Sightings are likely but never guaranteed.

nature.name: Tigers in the dry season
nature.what: As waterholes shrink in summer, tigers come out to drink and sightings peak in Bandhavgarh, Kanha, Ranthambore and Tadoba.
nature.tip: Book core-zone safaris months ahead on the official portal. It's hot: bring a scarf and water.

nature.name: One-horned rhinos, Kaziranga
nature.what: Two-thirds of the world's greater one-horned rhinos live here, along with wild buffalo, swamp deer and elephants on open grassland.
nature.tip: The park is closed in the monsoon. Book jeep safaris in different ranges: Central (Kohora) and Western (Bagori) are the best for rhinos.

nature.name: Asiatic lions of Gir
nature.what: The last wild Asiatic lions live in and around Gir forest; prides are often seen resting by tracks in the dry teak forest.
nature.tip: Gir is closed mid-June to mid-October. Book the jungle trail permits online as soon as the window opens.

nature.name: Elephants of the Kabini backwaters
nature.what: As the reservoir recedes in summer, its grassy banks draw some of Asia's largest gatherings of wild elephants, with tigers and leopards nearby.
nature.tip: Take the boat safari in the late afternoon for elephants along the shore.

nature.name: Hornbills of Pakke
nature.what: Pakke tiger reserve protects great, wreathed and oriental pied hornbills, guarded by the Nyishi community's nest adoption programme. The Pakke Paga Hornbill Festival is held in January.
nature.tip: Stay at Seijosa and go out at dawn, when hornbills fly to fruiting trees.

nature.name: Gulls at Yamuna Ghat, Delhi
nature.what: Every winter, brown-headed and black-headed gulls from Central Asia fill the Yamuna in central Delhi, with boatmen rowing among them at dawn.
nature.tip: Go at sunrise in fog season for the classic shot of boats and birds in mist. Don't feed them processed snacks.

nature.name: Black-necked cranes
nature.what: The rare black-necked crane winters in the high Sangti valley near Dirang and in Bhutan, and breeds in summer on the high lakes of Ladakh.
nature.tip: Sangti is a short drive from Dirang on the way to Tawang. Keep your distance; there are only a few here.

nature.name: Monsoon waterfalls of the Western Ghats
nature.what: Jog, Dudhsagar and Athirappilly are at their thundering best after weeks of rain, and many smaller falls appear only now.
nature.tip: Mornings are clearest. Watch from viewpoints: pools are dangerous in spate and many are closed to swimming.

nature.name: The frozen Zanskar (Chadar)
nature.what: In deep winter the Zanskar river freezes into a sheet of ice that locals and trekkers walk along, past frozen waterfalls in a deep gorge.
nature.tip: Only with a registered operator; there is a mandatory acclimatisation and medical check in Leh. Conditions vary each year.

nature.name: Frozen Pangong
nature.what: In February the high lake freezes solid and turns from blue to white; a frozen lake run is now held on it.
nature.tip: Nights fall below −25°C. Take the Changla road only with a local driver and check road status in Leh.

nature.name: Powder season in Gulmarg
nature.what: Gulmarg's gondola climbs to nearly 4,000 m, opening up some of Asia's best powder snow for skiing and snowshoeing.
nature.tip: Book the gondola tickets online. Phase 2 can close in storms, so keep a day in hand.

nature.name: Coffee blossom in Coorg
nature.peak: a week after the first March rain
nature.what: A few days after the first 'blossom showers', the coffee estates of Kodagu flower white overnight with a scent like jasmine. It lasts just a few days.
nature.tip: Stay on a plantation homestay in March and ask your hosts to call you when the rain comes.

nature.name: Flame of the forest
nature.what: Palash trees blaze bright orange across the plateaus of Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh just before Holi; the flowers were the original Holi colour.
nature.tip: Drive the plateau roads around Netarhat and Betla, or the forests near Pachmarhi.

nature.name: Darjeeling's first flush
nature.what: The year's first and most prized tea is plucked in spring, light and floral; estates open for tasting while the bushes are freshest.
nature.tip: Visit an estate on a weekday morning to see plucking, then do a cupping session. Spring also brings the clearest Kanchenjunga views.

nature.name: Sangai deer and floating islands
nature.what: Keibul Lamjao, the world's only floating national park, is home to the dancing deer, the sangai, which lives nowhere else in the wild.
nature.tip: Climb the watchtower at dawn. The Manipur Sangai Festival is held in late November.

nature.name: Dzukou valley lilies
nature.what: The rolling bamboo-grass valley on the Nagaland–Manipur border blooms with the endemic Dzukou lily in summer.
nature.tip: It's a steep 3–4 hour climb from Viswema or Zakhama. Overnight in the rest house and carry warm layers.

nature.name: Ganges river dolphins, Vikramshila
nature.what: The stretch of the Ganga near Bhagalpur is India's only sanctuary for the endangered, almost blind Gangetic dolphin.
nature.tip: Take a country boat from Barari ghat in the calm morning hours and look for their brief surfacing.

nature.name: Winter in the Sundarbans
nature.what: The world's largest mangrove forest, home to swimming tigers, saltwater crocodiles and kingfishers, is best explored by boat in the cool months.
nature.tip: Book a two-day boat trip with an overnight in a village lodge. Tiger sightings are rare; the creeks are the real show.

nature.name: Breeding birds of Tso Moriri
nature.what: Bar-headed geese, black-necked cranes and brown-headed gulls breed on this high lake in summer, among nomadic Changpa herders.
nature.tip: An Inner Line Permit is needed. Spend a night at Korzok; it's at 4,500 m, so arrive acclimatised.

nature.name: Dark skies of Hanle
nature.what: India's first dark-sky reserve: on clear moonless nights the Milky Way is bright enough to cast shadows.
nature.tip: Plan around the new moon. Village homestays have telescopes and trained 'astronomy ambassadors'.

nature.name: Monsoon green in the Nilgiris
nature.what: The Nilgiris turn emerald and misty in the monsoon, with tea gardens, shola forests and swollen streams at their freshest.
nature.tip: Ride the toy train when it's running and bring layers; Ooty is cold and damp.

journeys.name: Manali to Leh
journeys.why: One of the great high roads of the world: four high passes, two above 5,000 m, the Gata Loops, the high More Plains, and almost no villages between Darcha and Upshi.
journeys.best: Baralacha La to Tanglang La, across Sarchu and the More Plains
tips: Spend a night in Jispa or Sarchu rather than driving it in one go: altitude sickness is the main risk.
The road usually opens in June and closes with the first heavy snow in October; check status with the Border Roads Organisation.
Carry cash and fuel up at Tandi: there's no petrol pump for about 365 km.

stops.name: Manali
stops.note: Start early to beat Atal Tunnel traffic

stops.name: Jispa
stops.note: Good first night by the Bhaga river

stops.name: Sarchu
stops.note: Tent camps on the Himachal–Ladakh border

stops.name: Leh
stops.note: Rest a full day before going higher

journeys.name: Srinagar to Leh
journeys.why: The gentler way up to Ladakh, climbing from Kashmir's green meadows over Zojila into the moonscape of Ladakh, past Kargil and the old monasteries of Lamayuru and Alchi.
journeys.best: Zojila pass and the descent past Drass into the Suru valley
tips: Going this way first helps you acclimatise better than Manali–Leh.
Zojila closes in winter; the new tunnel under it is expected to open in early 2028.
Stop at the Kargil War Memorial in Drass, and overnight in Kargil.

journeys.name: The Spiti circuit
journeys.why: A loop through Kinnaur's apple orchards and gorges into the cold desert of Spiti, with thousand-year-old monasteries and villages above 4,000 m, out over Kunzum La.
journeys.best: Nako to Kaza along the Spiti river, and Kunzum La to Chandratal
tips: Go clockwise from Shimla to acclimatise gradually.
Indian citizens no longer need a permit for Kinnaur and Spiti; foreign visitors need one.
Kunzum La and the Batal road usually open in June; the Kinnaur side is open most of the year.

journeys.name: The Konkan coast
journeys.why: Sea forts, quiet beaches, temple towns and fish thalis along the coast south of Mumbai, slower and lovelier than the highway inland.
journeys.best: Ganpatipule to Tarkarli, with the Sindhudurg sea fort
tips: Ferries cross the creeks at several points (Dighi–Agardanda, Bagmandla–Veshvi); check timings locally.
Stay in homestays in Dapoli, Guhagar or Malvan and eat Malvani fish thalis.
Monsoon makes it gorgeous but rough; beaches are unsafe for swimming June–September.

journeys.name: Karnataka's temple coast
journeys.why: Wild beaches below the Western Ghats, the pilgrim town of Gokarna, the giant Shiva of Murudeshwar, Udupi's temple food and Mangaluru's seafood.
journeys.best: Gokarna to Murudeshwar, with the hills dropping straight into the sea
tips: Walk the beach trail from Kudle to Om, Half Moon and Paradise beaches in Gokarna.
Detour inland to Jog Falls after the monsoon.
Eat at Udupi's temple and try a Mangalorean fish thali.

journeys.name: East Coast Road to Puducherry
journeys.why: A short, easy coastal drive past Pallava shore temples and rock carvings at Mahabalipuram to the French Quarter of Puducherry and Auroville.
journeys.best: Mahabalipuram's shore temple at sunrise
tips: Leave Chennai early to reach Mahabalipuram before the heat and the crowds.
Stop at DakshinaChitra, a living museum of South Indian homes.
Avoid the north-east monsoon peak in November if you can.

journeys.name: Temple towns and Chettinad
journeys.why: The great Chola temples, the merchant mansions and kitchens of Chettinad, and the living temple city of Madurai.
journeys.best: The Chettinad villages around Karaikudi and Kanadukathan
tips: Stay in a restored Chettinad mansion and book a cooking session.
Brihadeeswarar is glorious in late-afternoon light.
Temple dress codes apply: cover shoulders and knees.

journeys.name: Rajasthan's desert cities
journeys.why: The classic royal route: the pink city, the blue city, the golden fort rising from the Thar, and the lakes of Udaipur, with stepwells and Jain temples between.
journeys.best: Jodhpur to Jaisalmer across the Thar, and the Aravalli road to Ranakpur
tips: Spend a night in the dunes beyond Sam or Khuri, away from the crowded camps.
Drive Jodhpur–Ranakpur–Udaipur through the Aravallis rather than the highway.
Winter nights in the desert drop near freezing; pack layers.

journeys.name: Kutch: salt, crafts and ruins
journeys.why: The blinding white salt desert under a full moon, embroidery and weaving villages, and the Harappan city of Dholavira on the edge of the Rann.
journeys.best: The Road to Heaven across the Rann to Dholavira
tips: Time it with a full moon for the White Rann at night.
A permit for the Rann is issued online or at Bhirandiyara.
Buy crafts directly from artisans in Bhujodi, Hodka and Nirona.

journeys.name: Guwahati to Tawang
journeys.why: From the Brahmaputra plains up through Monpa villages and over the 4,170 m Sela pass to the great monastery of Tawang.
journeys.best: Dirang to Tawang over Sela, now with the Sela tunnel as an all-weather option
tips: You need an Inner Line Permit, which you can get online.
October–November is also excellent; avoid the monsoon (June–September) when landslides are common.
Break the journey at Bomdila or Dirang both ways.

journeys.name: Meghalaya loop
journeys.why: Living root bridges, plunging waterfalls, the clearest river in India and Khasi villages, on short drives through the clouds.
journeys.best: Sohra's cliffs and the drive down to Dawki on the Bangladesh border
tips: The double-decker root bridge at Nongriat is about 3,500 steps down and back; start early.
Boating on the Umngot at Dawki is best from November to April, when the water is clear.
Monsoon is spectacular but foggy; roads stay open.

journeys.name: North Sikkim
journeys.why: From Gangtok up the Teesta to Lachung's apple orchards, the rhododendron valley of Yumthang, and the sacred high lake of Gurudongmar at about 5,400 m.
journeys.best: Lachen to Gurudongmar at dawn
tips: Permits are arranged by registered Gangtok tour operators only; you can't self-drive.
October–November brings clear skies; landslides often close roads in the monsoon.
Gurudongmar is very high: don't stay long and descend if you feel unwell.

journeys.name: Kerala: hills to backwaters
journeys.why: Fort Kochi's old streets, the tea hills of Munnar, the spice forests of Thekkady, and a night on a houseboat in the backwaters.
journeys.best: The climb into Munnar through tea gardens and waterfalls
tips: Book a houseboat that cruises the quieter Kuttanad canals, not just Vembanad lake.
Eravikulam park closes for a few weeks in spring for the Nilgiri tahr calving season.
Monsoon (June–August) is lush and cheap but wet.

journeys.name: Nilgiri Mountain Railway
journeys.why: A UNESCO-listed metre-gauge rack railway that climbs about 2,000 m through tea gardens, tunnels and viaducts, pushed by steam on the steepest stretch.
journeys.best: Mettupalayam to Coonoor, the steep rack section
tips: Book weeks ahead on IRCTC; first class has the best views on the right side going up.
The morning train from Mettupalayam is the classic ride; take the road back.
Services can be suspended after landslides in the monsoon.

journeys.name: Kalka–Shimla Railway
journeys.why: A UNESCO-listed narrow-gauge line built in 1903, with over 100 tunnels and hundreds of bridges climbing into the hills to the old summer capital.
journeys.best: Barog, with its long tunnel and station café, and the curves above Solan
tips: Book the Shivalik Deluxe or Himalayan Queen early on IRCTC.
Snow on the line in winter makes a magical ride; check for delays.
Sit on the right side going up for the valley views.

journeys.name: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway
journeys.days: About 7 hours end to end; or the 2-hour joy ride
journeys.why: The original 'toy train', a UNESCO site from 1881, zigzagging and looping up through bazaars and tea gardens to Darjeeling.
journeys.best: Ghum, the highest station, and the Batasia Loop with Kanchenjunga behind it
tips: The steam joy ride from Darjeeling to Ghum and back is the easiest way to ride it.
Clear mountain views are most likely October–December and in spring.
Book on IRCTC; joy rides sell out in season.

journeys.name: Konkan Railway in the monsoon
journeys.why: Through the Western Ghats through about 90 tunnels and high viaducts over swollen rivers, past waterfalls that appear only in the rain.
journeys.best: Ratnagiri to Kudal, and the Panval viaduct
tips: Some trains on the route have Vistadome coaches with glass roofs; book them early.
Take a day train for the views.
Monsoon timetables apply from June to October, with slower speeds.

journeys.name: Katra to Srinagar by train
journeys.why: India's most dramatic new line: across the Chenab bridge, the world's highest railway arch, and the Anji Khad cable-stayed bridge, then through the Pir Panjal into the Kashmir valley.
journeys.best: The Chenab and Anji bridges, and emerging from the Banihal tunnel into the valley
tips: Book the Vande Bharat on IRCTC; carry ID for security checks at stations.
Snow in winter makes the valley section beautiful; trains usually run.
Sit on the left from Katra for the Chenab bridge.

journeys.name: Past Dudhsagar on the Goa–Londa line
journeys.why: The line climbs the Braganza Ghat and passes right in front of the four-tiered Dudhsagar falls, at their fullest after the monsoon.
journeys.best: The bridge in front of Dudhsagar falls
tips: Sit on the right going from Goa towards Londa.
Walking on the tracks is banned and dangerous; see the falls from the train or by jeep from Kulem after the rains.
Check which trains run on this line, as timetables change.

journeys.name: Across the sea to Rameswaram
journeys.why: The rail line runs onto Pamban island over the sea on the new Pamban bridge, India's first vertical-lift sea bridge, beside the old 1914 bridge. The road then continues to the ghost town of Dhanushkodi.
journeys.best: The two-kilometre crossing of the Palk Strait
tips: Look out for the old cantilever bridge alongside.
Dhanushkodi is best in the early morning; the land's-end road is open in daylight only.
Visit the Ramanathaswamy temple corridors in the early morning.

h36.intro: Boulder hills, a ruined imperial city and a slow river: Hampi rewards early mornings and lazy afternoons.
eat: Thali on a banana leaf in Hampi Bazaar
Fresh lime soda in a riverside café
h36.stay: Hampi village for atmosphere, or Kamalapura and Hosapete for more comfortable hotels.
h36.tip: Hire a cycle or e-bike for the day; distances between sites are bigger than they look.
sat: Climb Matanga Hill for sunrise over the boulders and the Virupaksha gopuram.
Walk the old Hampi Bazaar to the Virupaksha Temple, still in worship after 1,300 years, and watch the morning rituals.
Cycle or take an auto to the Vittala Temple and its stone chariot; tap the musical pillars only where allowed.
Long lunch and rest in the shade: the midday heat is fierce.
The Royal Enclosure, the stepped tank and the Lotus Mahal in the soft late light.
Sunset from Hemakuta Hill among the early temples.
sun: Coracle ride on the Tungabhadra from the ferry point near Virupapur Gaddi.
Achyutaraya Temple and the walk along the river to Vittala, almost empty at this hour.
Hampi Archaeological Museum at Kamalapura for the scale models and sculpture.
Out to Anegundi village, older than Hampi, for the Kishkindha legends and banana-fibre crafts.

h36.intro: Yellow French villas, Tamil temples and a seafront promenade, with Auroville's forests just up the road.
eat: Croissants and baguettes from French-style bakeries
Filter coffee in the Tamil Quarter
h36.stay: White Town heritage guesthouses, or a quieter stay near Auroville.
h36.tip: Rent a scooter for Auroville and the beaches; White Town itself is best on foot.
sat: Walk the Promenade at sunrise, when it's car-free and full of joggers.
Breakfast in White Town, then wander Rue Romain Rolland and Rue Dumas among the colonial villas.
Sri Aurobindo Ashram (quiet, no photos inside).
The Tamil Quarter's verandah houses and the Manakula Vinayagar temple.
Dinner and an evening on the Promenade.
sun: Drive to Auroville; book the Matrimandir viewing point at the Visitors' Centre.
Auroville cafés and craft shops, then back via Serenity Beach.
Paradise Beach by boat from Chunnambar backwaters.

h36.intro: Palaces reflected in lakes, rooftop dinners and the Aravalli hills all around.
h36.stay: Around Lal Ghat and Gangaur Ghat for lake views, walkable to the palace.
h36.tip: Lake levels vary with the monsoon; boats and views are best September to February.
sat: City Palace, the largest palace complex in Rajasthan, before the tour groups.
Jagdish Temple and the lanes down to Gangaur Ghat.
Boat on Lake Pichola to Jag Mandir.
Sunset from Ambrai Ghat with the palace lit across the water.
Dharohar folk dance at Bagore ki Haveli.
sun: Sajjangarh Monsoon Palace for views over the lakes (or Fateh Sagar at dawn).
Saheliyon ki Bari's fountains and gardens.
A day trip to Ranakpur's marble Jain temple and Kumbhalgarh's walls if you have a car.

h36.intro: A golden sandstone fort that people still live in, carved havelis, and a night in the Thar.
h36.stay: Outside the fort, to reduce pressure on its fragile walls; or a desert camp.
h36.tip: Choose a smaller camp away from the main Sam strip for real silence and stars.
sat: Walk up into Jaisalmer Fort as the stone glows in the morning sun.
Patwon ki Haveli and Nathmal ki Haveli's carved facades.
Lunch, then Gadisar Lake and its ghats.
Drive out to the dunes beyond Sam or Khuri for sunset and a night camp.
sun: Kuldhara's abandoned village and the Bada Bagh cenotaphs.
Sunset from Vyas Chhatri, looking back at the fort.

h36.intro: The blue city beneath one of India's mightiest forts.
eat: Pyaaz kachori and mirchi bada near the clock tower
h36.stay: Near the clock tower or in Brahmpuri haveli guesthouses with fort views.
h36.tip: Walk down from Mehrangarh through the old city lanes instead of taking a tuk-tuk; it's the best part of Jodhpur.
sat: Mehrangarh Fort and its museum; the audio guide is excellent.
Jaswant Thada's white marble memorial, with the fort rising behind it.
Walk down through the blue houses of Brahmpuri to the Toorji ka Jhalra stepwell.
Clock tower and Sardar Market at dusk.
sun: Rao Jodha Desert Rock Park's trails below the fort.
Mandore gardens, or a Bishnoi village safari.

h36.intro: Forts on the ridges, a planned pink old city and the best crafts shopping in India.
h36.stay: Inside or near the walled city, in a haveli guesthouse.
h36.tip: Buy a composite ticket for the main monuments.
sat: Amber Fort early, before the heat and crowds.
Panna Meena ka Kund stepwell and the Jal Mahal viewpoint.
City Palace and Jantar Mantar's giant instruments.
Hawa Mahal from a café across the road, then the bazaars of Johari and Bapu.
Sunset from Nahargarh Fort over the city.
sun: Block printing in Sanganer or Bagru.
Galta Ji, the monkey temple in a gorge.

h36.intro: The oldest living city, where life and death meet on the ghats of the Ganga.
h36.stay: A ghat-side guesthouse between Assi and Dashashwamedh.
h36.tip: Manikarnika's burning ghat is sacred: watch respectfully, no photos.
sat: Boat ride from Assi Ghat at sunrise along the ghats.
Kachori-sabzi and jalebi breakfast in the lanes.
Walk the lanes to the Kashi Vishwanath corridor.
Visit Banarasi silk weavers in the weaving quarters of Madanpura or Peeli Kothi.
Ganga aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat; watch from a boat for the best view.
sun: Morning aarti at Assi Ghat, then a walk north along the ghats.
Sarnath, where the Buddha gave his first sermon.

h36.intro: Yoga capital at the foot of the Himalaya, with rapids, ashrams and evening aarti.
h36.stay: Tapovan or Laxman Jhula for cafés; Swarg Ashram side for calm.
h36.tip: Rishikesh is vegetarian and alcohol-free by law.
sat: Walk across the Ram Jhula footbridge and the cafés of Tapovan.
Ganga aarti at Parmarth Niketan or Triveni Ghat.
sun: The Beatles Ashram (Chaurasi Kutia) and its murals.
Kunjapuri temple for Himalayan views at sunset.

h36.intro: The Golden Temple's serenity, the drama at the border and some of India's best food.
h36.stay: Close to the Golden Temple so you can visit at night and at dawn.
h36.tip: Cover your head and remove shoes; scarves are provided.
sat: The Golden Temple in the pre-dawn hours as the Guru Granth Sahib is carried in.
Kulcha breakfast in the old city.
Jallianwala Bagh and the Partition Museum.
Help in the Golden Temple's langar kitchen.
Beating Retreat at the Attari–Wagah border; arrive early.
sun: The Golden Temple in daylight, and its museum.

h36.intro: Beyond the Taj: Mughal forts, a jewel-box tomb and Fatehpur Sikri.
h36.stay: Near the Taj's east gate.
h36.tip: Buy Taj tickets online to skip queues.
sat: The Taj Mahal at sunrise; it's closed on Fridays.
Sunset at Mehtab Bagh across the Yamuna.

h36.intro: Nawabi architecture, chikankari and the best kebabs in India.
h36.stay: Hazratganj for comfort and walkability.
h36.tip: Food is best in the old city at night.
sat: Bara Imambara and its Bhool Bhulaiya labyrinth.
Rumi Darwaza and the Chota Imambara.
Kebab lunch in Aminabad or Chowk.

h36.intro: A sleepy town of Bundela palaces and cenotaphs on the Betwa river.
h36.stay: Near the fort or along the Betwa.
h36.tip: The light-and-sound show at the fort is in the evening.
sat: Jahangir Mahal and Raja Mahal in the fort complex.
Ram Raja Temple, where Ram is worshipped as a king.
Chaturbhuj Temple: climb to the roof.
Sunset at the cenotaphs (chhatris) on the Betwa.
sun: Kayaking or rafting on the Betwa.
Day trip to Jhansi Fort or Datia Palace.

h36.intro: Exquisite Chandela temples carved with the whole of life.
h36.stay: Near the Western Group.
h36.tip: Khajuraho Dance Festival is in February.
sat: The Western Group at opening, when the sandstone glows.

h36.intro: Tea gardens, colonial cafés and Kanchenjunga from Tiger Hill.
h36.stay: Near Chowrasta, walkable to everything.
h36.tip: Clear views are best October–December; carry warm layers.
sat: Tiger Hill for sunrise on Kanchenjunga.
Batasia Loop and Ghoom Monastery on the way back.
Happy Valley Tea Estate: plucking and tasting.
Himalayan Mountaineering Institute and the zoo.
Chowrasta Mall and tea at a colonial café.
sun: Toy train joy ride to Ghum.

h36.intro: A clean, walkable hill capital with monasteries and Kanchenjunga.
h36.stay: Around MG Marg.
h36.tip: Permits for Tsomgo/Nathula take a day; arrange on arrival.
sat: Tashi viewpoint for Kanchenjunga at dawn.
sun: Tsomgo Lake and Nathula (permit through an operator).

h36.intro: The Scotland of the East: pine hills, music cafés and waterfalls.
h36.stay: Police Bazar or Laitumkhrah.
h36.tip: Many shops close on Sundays; plan Sohra or Laitlum for that day.
sat: Don Bosco Museum of indigenous cultures.
Live music in Police Bazar's cafés.
sun: Day trip to Sohra: Nohkalikai, Mawsmai cave, Seven Sisters falls.

h36.intro: Colonial grandeur, adda culture and India's best sweets.
h36.stay: Park Street or near Esplanade.
h36.tip: Durga Puja (October) is magical and packed.
sat: Mullick Ghat flower market under Howrah Bridge at dawn.
sun: College Street books and Indian Coffee House.
Jorasanko Thakurbari, Tagore's family home, and the Marble Palace (get the free pass from the tourism office first).
New Market and Esplanade street food.

h36.intro: A temple town with a string of cliff-bound beaches.
h36.stay: Kudle or Om beach huts, or a guesthouse in town.
h36.tip: Respect the temple town's customs; avoid swimming in the monsoon.
sat: Mahabaleshwar Temple and the town's chariot street.
sun: Trek to Half Moon and Paradise beaches.

h36.intro: Palaces, silk and Karnataka's grandest festival.
h36.stay: Near the palace.
h36.tip: Dasara (Sept–Oct) is spectacular but book far ahead.
sat: Devaraja Market for flowers and spices.
Chamundi Hill and the Nandi monolith.
Palace illumination (Sundays and holidays, about 7–7:45 pm).

h36.intro: A layered port town of Chinese nets, spice warehouses and art.
eat: Fresh catch from the nets, cooked nearby
h36.stay: Fort Kochi heritage homestays.
h36.tip: The Kochi-Muziris Biennale runs in some winters.
sat: St Francis Church and Santa Cruz Basilica.
Mattancherry Palace and Jew Town's Paradesi Synagogue.
Kathakali performance (arrive early for the make-up).

h36.intro: Kerala's backwater capital, best seen slowly from the water.
h36.stay: A houseboat, or a homestay in Kuttanad.
h36.tip: Nehru Trophy Boat Race is in August.
sat: Board a houseboat for an overnight cruise.
Lunch on board: karimeen and Kerala sadya.
Village life along the Kuttanad canals.

h36.intro: A temple city that never sleeps, built around the vast Meenakshi Amman Temple and its towering gopurams.
h36.stay: Near the temple.
h36.tip: Phones and cameras aren't allowed inside the Meenakshi temple; leave them at the counter. Cover shoulders and legs.
sat: Gandhi Memorial Museum, which holds the blood-stained cloth he wore when he was shot.
The Palliyarai ceremony, when Sundareswarar is carried to Meenakshi's chamber for the night.
sun: Soft idlis with several chutneys at one of the city's famous idli shops.
Thiruparankundram, a temple cut into a rock hill.
The flower market at Mattuthavani, one of the biggest in the south.
A glass of jigarthanda and kothu parotta on the streets.

h36.intro: A high-desert town of monasteries and mud-brick palaces, ringed by mountains. Take it slowly.
h36.stay: Changspa or the old town.
h36.tip: Leh is at about 3,500 m. If you fly in, rest the whole first day and only go higher (Khardung La, Pangong) from day three.
sat: Arrive, drink lots of water and rest; don't climb or exert yourself on day one.
A slow walk through Leh's old town and the Main Bazaar.
Shanti Stupa for sunset over the valley (drive up if you're breathless).
sun: Thiksey Monastery's morning prayers, with monks blowing long horns from the roof.
Shey Palace's giant Buddha on the way back.
Hemis, the largest monastery in Ladakh, and its museum.
Leh Palace, then the Hall of Fame war museum.

h36.intro: Home of the Dalai Lama and the Tibetan government in exile, under the snowy Dhauladhar range.
h36.stay: McLeod Ganj or Dharamkot.
h36.tip: The weather turns quickly; carry a rain layer even on sunny days.
sat: The Tsuglagkhang complex, the Dalai Lama's temple, and the Tibet Museum beside it.
Walk to Bhagsunag temple and the waterfall above it.
Up to Dharamkot's cafés and yoga studios in the deodars.
The kora path around Tsuglagkhang at dusk, with prayer wheels and pilgrims.
sun: Hike to Triund ridge for the Dhauladhar wall up close (about 3 hours up).
Norbulingka Institute in lower Dharamshala, where Tibetan arts are taught and practised.
Sunset from St John in the Wilderness church.

cur.name: The skeleton lake
cur.story: Hundreds of human skeletons lie around a glacial lake at 5,000 m. DNA studies found they died in at least two separate events about a thousand years apart, including a group from the eastern Mediterranean. Trekking rules change, so check current permits.

cur.name: Bridges that grow
cur.story: Khasi villagers train the roots of rubber fig trees across streams until they become bridges strong enough for dozens of people; some are said to be centuries old and still growing.

cur.name: The village without doors
cur.story: Houses here traditionally have no doors or locks, as villagers believe Lord Shani protects them from theft.

cur.name: The hill that pulls cars uphill
cur.story: On the Leh–Kargil road a stretch appears to roll cars uphill in neutral. It's an optical illusion: the road actually slopes slightly down.

cur.name: The whistling village
cur.story: Every person in Kongthong has a melody, a 'jingrwai iawbei', given by their mother at birth and used like a name to call across the valleys.

cur.name: The hanging pillar
cur.story: One of the 70 pillars in Lepakshi's Veerabhadra temple barely touches the floor; visitors slide cloth under it.

cur.name: Where birds fall from the sky
cur.story: On dark, misty nights in September and October, disoriented birds fly towards lights in this Dima Hasao village, a phenomenon still not fully explained.

cur.name: An island that keeps shrinking
cur.story: Once among the world's largest river islands, Majuli has lost much of its land to Brahmaputra erosion. Its Vaishnavite satras still keep up masked dance and theatre.

cur.name: A meteor crater lake
cur.story: A meteorite struck the Deccan basalt tens of thousands of years ago (estimates vary), leaving a 1.8 km crater with a salty, alkaline lake that turned pink in 2020 from microbes.

cur.name: The fort you mustn't visit at night
cur.story: Legends of a curse surround this ruined 17th-century town; the Archaeological Survey bars entry after sunset.

cur.name: The village abandoned in one night
cur.story: Paliwal Brahmins are said to have abandoned Kuldhara and 83 other villages overnight two centuries ago, cursing anyone who tried to settle there.

cur.name: The temple of rats
cur.story: At Deshnoke thousands of rats are fed and protected as holy; seeing a rare white one is a blessing.

cur.name: The 3,500-step stepwell
cur.story: Thirteen storeys of criss-crossing steps descend into one of India's deepest stepwells, built over a thousand years ago.

cur.name: The musical pillars
cur.story: The slender granite pillars of Hampi's Vittala Temple ring with different notes when tapped; tapping is now restricted to protect them.

cur.name: The whispering gallery
cur.story: Under the vast dome of Gol Gumbaz, a whisper on one side of the gallery is heard clearly 37 metres away, and claps echo several times.

cur.name: The pillar that won't rust
cur.story: The 1,600-year-old iron pillar at the Qutub complex has barely corroded, thanks to its high phosphorus content and a protective film.

cur.name: The stone clock
cur.story: The carved wheels of the Konark Sun Temple act as sundials: the shadow of the spokes tells the time to within minutes.

cur.name: A temple carved top-down
cur.story: Ellora's Kailasa temple was cut downwards from a single basalt hill, removing an estimated 200,000 tonnes of rock.

cur.name: Krishna's butterball
cur.story: A 250-tonne boulder at Mahabalipuram rests on a slope at an impossible angle; in 1908 the governor of Madras tried to have it hauled away with seven elephants, and it didn't budge.

cur.name: The bricks that float
cur.story: The 13th-century Ramappa temple's roof was built with bricks so light they float on water.

cur.name: The church in the reservoir
cur.story: A Gothic church submerged by a dam reappears each summer when water levels drop.

cur.name: The town the sea took
cur.story: A cyclone in 1964 wiped out this busy port; the ruins of its church, station and post office still stand at land's end.

cur.name: The eternal fire
cur.story: Cremation fires on Varanasi's Manikarnika Ghat are said to have burned without pause for thousands of years.

cur.name: The labyrinth
cur.story: The Bhool Bhulaiya above Lucknow's Bara Imambara has around 1,000 passages; a guide is advised.

cur.name: A mud volcano
cur.story: On Baratang island, small volcanoes bubble mud, near limestone caves reached by mangrove creeks.

cur.name: The sea that walks away
cur.story: At low tide the sea at Chandipur recedes up to five kilometres, so you can walk out on the seabed.

cur.name: Boats that seem to fly
cur.story: In winter the Umngot river is so clear that boats appear to hover above the stones beneath them.

cur.name: The cleanest village
cur.story: Mawlynnong has bamboo dustbins, flower-lined paths and a famous community cleanliness routine.

cur.name: The ghost lights of the Rann
cur.story: Locals tell of chir batti, dancing lights over the salt flats on dark nights; scientists suspect marsh gas.

cur.name: The land of floating islands
cur.story: Loktak Lake is dotted with phumdis, floating mats of soil and vegetation, some with fishermen's huts on them.

cur.name: The colour-changing lake
cur.story: Pangong's water changes from blue to green to grey with the light; it is salt water yet freezes in winter.

cur.name: The lake that is a pilgrimage
cur.story: Legend says Guru Padmasambhava blessed part of this high lake so that it would never fully freeze.

cur.name: The Paradesi Synagogue
cur.story: Built in 1568, it is the oldest active synagogue in the Commonwealth, with Chinese tiles and Belgian chandeliers.

cur.name: The Harappan city in the salt desert
cur.story: Dholavira, a UNESCO site, was a planned Harappan city with stepped reservoirs cut into rock to store every drop of rain, and the remains of a large signboard written in the still-undeciphered Indus script.

exp.name: Block printing in Bagru
exp.what: Spend a morning with the chhipa families of Bagru, who still print cloth with carved wooden blocks and natural dyes like indigo, pomegranate and iron rust. Many workshops let you print your own fabric.

exp.name: Blue pottery in Jaipur
exp.what: Jaipur's blue pottery is made from quartz paste, not clay, and painted in cobalt and turquoise. Small studios on the Amer road run short hands-on sessions.

exp.name: A night in the Thar
exp.what: Ride a camel or a jeep out beyond the busy camps to open dunes, eat dinner by a fire with folk musicians and sleep under a sky full of stars.

exp.name: Bishnoi village safari
exp.what: Visit the Bishnoi villages outside Jodhpur, a community that has protected blackbuck and khejri trees for 500 years, with potters, weavers and an opium-free 'amal' ceremony welcome.

exp.name: Kutch craft trail
exp.what: Meet the weavers of Bhujodi, the rogan painters of Nirona and the embroiderers of Hodka and Dhordo; buy directly from the people who make the work.

exp.name: Rann Utsav
exp.what: A tent city on the edge of the White Rann with folk music, crafts and full-moon nights on the salt, from November to February.

exp.name: A houseboat night
exp.what: Board a kettuvallam rice barge converted into a floating home, drift through paddy fields and villages, and eat Kerala meals cooked on board.

exp.name: Kathakali make-up session
exp.what: At Fort Kochi's Kathakali theatres, arrive an hour early to watch dancers paint their faces green, red and white before the performance.

exp.name: Kalaripayattu
exp.what: Watch Kerala's ancient martial art, with leaps, staff fights and sword-and-shield sequences, at evening shows in Thekkady and Kochi.

exp.name: Spice plantation walk
exp.what: Walk among cardamom, pepper vines, cinnamon and nutmeg in the hills around Thekkady, and buy straight from the farm.

exp.name: Chettinad cooking
exp.what: Learn the fiery Chettinad style of cooking, with freshly ground spices, in a merchant mansion around Karaikudi.

exp.name: Kanchipuram silk weaving
exp.what: Watch weavers on pit looms making heavy silk saris with gold zari borders, and learn how to spot real Kanchipuram silk.

exp.name: Coracle ride
exp.what: Float on the Tungabhadra in a round bamboo-and-tarp coracle, spun gently past the boulders and riverside shrines.

exp.name: Coffee estate stay
exp.what: Stay on a family-run estate in Kodagu, walk the plantation with the planter, and drink coffee grown, roasted and brewed on the spot.

exp.name: Channapatna toy workshop
exp.what: Watch craftsmen turn ivory-wood toys on lathes and colour them with lac, a craft dating back to Tipu Sultan's time.

exp.name: Yakshagana night
exp.what: Coastal Karnataka's all-night dance-drama, with huge headdresses and drums, performed in temple grounds and open fields in the dry season.

exp.name: Goa spice farm
exp.what: Tour a spice plantation near Ponda with a buffet lunch of Goan Hindu cooking.

exp.name: Fontainhas walk
exp.what: Walk the Latin quarter of Panaji, with its brightly painted Portuguese houses, azulejo tiles and old taverns.

exp.name: Paithani weaving at Yeola
exp.what: Visit the looms of Yeola and Paithan where Paithani silk saris with peacock and lotus borders are woven, some taking months to finish.

exp.name: Wine country at Nashik
exp.what: Tour the vineyards of India's wine capital in the harvest season, with tastings and sunset views over the vines.

exp.name: Kumartuli idol makers
exp.what: In the lanes of north Kolkata, sculptors shape clay and straw into the goddesses of Durga Puja; visit in the weeks before the festival.

exp.name: Darjeeling tea tasting
exp.what: See plucking and processing at a tea estate, then taste the difference between first-flush, second-flush and autumn teas.

exp.name: Baul music at Shantiniketan
exp.what: Hear the wandering Baul minstrels of Bengal, especially during the Poush Mela fair in December.

exp.name: Sundarbans by boat
exp.what: Two days on a country boat through mangrove creeks, with nights in a village lodge and the faint chance of a swimming tiger.

exp.name: Pattachitra at Raghurajpur
exp.what: A whole village of painters near Puri, where every house is a studio for pattachitra scroll painting and palm-leaf engraving.

exp.name: Majuli mask making
exp.what: At Samaguri Satra, monks make the bamboo and clay masks used in Vaishnavite theatre, some large enough to cover the whole body.

exp.name: A tea bungalow stay
exp.what: Stay in a colonial planter's bungalow on an Assam tea estate, walk the gardens at plucking time and taste strong Assam CTC and orthodox teas.

exp.name: Living root bridge trek
exp.what: Descend about 3,500 steps through the jungle to Nongriat's double-decker root bridge and the blue pools beyond.

exp.name: Hornbill Festival
exp.what: Nagaland's 'festival of festivals', 1–10 December, brings all the Naga tribes together for dances, songs, games and food at Kisama heritage village.

exp.name: Khonoma green village
exp.what: India's first 'green village', where the Angami community banned hunting and logging; walk the terraced fields and stay with a family.

exp.name: Rafting the Ganga
exp.what: Raft the rapids from Shivpuri to Rishikesh with named rapids like 'The Wall' and 'Roller Coaster'. Season September to June.

exp.name: Paragliding at Bir Billing
exp.what: Fly tandem from Billing, one of the world's top paragliding sites, landing among the Tibetan colony and tea gardens of Bir.

exp.name: A Spiti homestay
exp.what: Stay with a family in a high Spiti village, eat thukpa and tsampa, and search for fossils on the slopes around Langza.

exp.name: Skiing in Gulmarg
exp.what: Ski Asia's highest gondola-served slopes, with instructors and gear for every level.

exp.name: Dal Lake floating market
exp.what: Take a shikara at dawn to the vegetable market that trades from boats in the middle of Dal Lake.

exp.name: Hemis festival
exp.what: Masked cham dances in the monastery courtyard celebrate Guru Padmasambhava's birthday, in June or July.

exp.name: Stargazing at Hanle
exp.what: Look through telescopes with local 'astronomy ambassadors' in India's first dark-sky reserve.

exp.name: Ganga aarti by boat
exp.what: Watch the evening aarti from a boat on the river, as priests wave great brass lamps in unison.

exp.name: Chikankari in Lucknow
exp.what: See women embroider delicate white-on-white chikankari in the old quarters of Chowk.

exp.name: Gond art in Bhopal
exp.what: Discover the dot-and-line art of the Gond people at Bharat Bhavan and the Tribal Museum, and meet painters who sell their work.

exp.name: Maheshwar weavers
exp.what: Watch handloom weavers making light Maheshwari saris in the shadow of Ahilya Fort on the Narmada.

exp.name: Madhubani painting
exp.what: Visit Ranti and Jitwarpur villages, where women paint the bold Mithila style on paper, cloth and walls.

exp.name: Golden Temple langar
exp.what: Help peel, chop and serve in one of the world's biggest free kitchens, which feeds tens of thousands every day.

exp.name: Beating Retreat at Attari
exp.what: The daily border ceremony with high-kicking guards and roaring crowds, an hour from Amritsar.

exp.name: Pochampally ikat
exp.what: See the tie-and-dye ikat process, where threads are dyed before weaving into geometric patterns.

exp.name: Araku coffee trail
exp.what: Ride the train up to Araku valley, visit coffee farms run by tribal cooperatives and try their award-winning coffee.

exp.name: Kondapalli toys
exp.what: Watch artisans carve and paint light wooden toys of village scenes and gods.

exp.name: Scuba at Havelock
exp.what: Learn to dive or do a fun dive on the coral reefs off Swaraj Dweep (Havelock).

exp.name: Snorkelling in Lakshadweep
exp.what: Snorkel in turquoise coral lagoons on the few islands open to visitors (permit needed).

exp.name: Ima Keithel
exp.what: Asia's largest women-run market, centuries old, where only married women can trade.

exp.name: Ziro Festival of Music
exp.what: An outdoor indie music festival in the paddy fields of the Apatani valley, usually in late September.

exp.name: Old Delhi food walk
exp.what: Parathas, kebabs, jalebis and nihari in the lanes around Chandni Chowk and Jama Masjid.

best.title: New ways in
best.intro: Openings that change how you get somewhere.

items.name: Noida International Airport (Jewar)
items.why: Opened for passengers in June 2026. A new gateway to Agra, Mathura and Vrindavan that skips Delhi's traffic.

items.name: Navi Mumbai International Airport
items.why: Mumbai's second airport, opened in 2025, with more airlines adding flights. Handy for Alibag and the Konkan coast.

items.name: Vande Bharat sleepers
items.why: India's first sleeper Vande Bharat started on Howrah–Kamakhya in January 2026, and Bengaluru–Mumbai followed in November 2026. Overnight trains are back in style.

items.name: Kashmir by train
items.why: Trains now run all the way from Katra to Srinagar over the Chenab bridge, the world's highest rail arch.

items.name: The new Pamban bridge
items.why: India's first vertical-lift sea bridge, opened in 2025, carries trains to Rameswaram.

items.name: Rail to Mizoram
items.why: The Bairabi–Sairang line, opened in 2025, brought trains close to Aizawl for the first time.

items.name: Kashmir valley
items.why: Easier to reach than ever by train, and gorgeous in every season, from tulips in April to snow in January.

items.name: Tawang
items.why: The Sela tunnel keeps the road open in winter; go for the monastery and the Monpa villages.

items.name: Hanle
items.why: India's first dark-sky reserve, with village astronomers and some of the darkest skies on earth.

items.name: Rameswaram and Dhanushkodi
items.why: Ride the train over the new sea bridge, then go to land's end.

items.name: Majuli
items.why: The river island's satras, masks and monasteries, before more of it is lost to the Brahmaputra.

items.name: Kutch
items.why: The White Rann, craft villages and a UNESCO Harappan city, all in one winter trip.

items.name: Gandikota
items.why: India's 'grand canyon': a gorge of the Pennar river with a fort on its rim.

items.name: Chitrakote
items.why: India's widest waterfall, in tribal Bastar; most dramatic in the monsoon.

items.name: Mawlynnong and Dawki
items.why: Clear rivers, root bridges and spotless villages.

items.name: Ziro
items.why: Pine-ringed rice valleys of the Apatani people.

items.name: Gurez
items.why: A remote valley near the Line of Control, with wooden villages and the Kishanganga river.

items.name: Bhitarkanika
items.why: Mangroves with India's largest saltwater crocodiles.

best.title: Coming soon
best.intro: Projects to watch; go now, or wait for them.

items.name: Zojila tunnel
items.why: A 13 km tunnel under Zojila is expected to open in early 2028, making Srinagar–Leh an all-year road.

items.name: Mumbai–Ahmedabad bullet train
items.why: The first high-speed service on the corridor is targeted for August 2027.

uttar-pradesh:1: Shoot across the river with the Taj catching the evening sun; the garden stays open on Fridays, when the Taj itself is closed.
Be first in the queue at the east gate and frame the Taj through the gate arch, before the crowd fills the gardens.
rajasthan:2: A rooftop café across the street
The facade faces east, so the honeycomb windows glow pink in the first sun.
rajasthan:1: On still mornings the fort reflects in the lake; walk down the path from the parking area.
rajasthan:102: The palace and the lake turn gold, then the lights come on.
rajasthan:52: Frame the fort's golden walls behind the sandstone cenotaphs.
rajasthan:41: Look down on the blue houses of Brahmpuri in soft light.
uttar-pradesh:28: Drift from Assi towards Dashashwamedh as pilgrims bathe and the ghats light up.
karnataka:5: Watch the first light break over a landscape of boulders and temples.
karnataka:1: Silhouettes of early temples with the Virupaksha gopuram behind.
punjab:1: The marble walkway around the pool
Reflections are calmest and the gold glows under the lights.
odisha:1: The temple was aligned with the rising sun; the carved wheels are best in low side-light.
karnataka:101: The lawns inside the main gate
Nearly 100,000 bulbs light up the palace; arrive at 6:45 pm.
west-bengal:1: Catch the white marble in the last light, reflected in the water.
west-bengal:10: Marigold sellers and bathers with the bridge above.
west-bengal:77: Kanchenjunga turns pink, then gold; clearest October to December.
ladakh:2: The Leh valley, the palace and the Stok range in warm light.
ladakh:7: Monks blow conch shells for morning prayers; ask before photographing people.
ladakh:36: The water shifts through shades of blue as clouds move.
jammu-and-kashmir:1: Head to the floating market and photograph traders in the mist.
kerala:44: Clouds below you over the world's highest tea estate; jeeps leave Suryanelli around 4:30 am.
tamil-nadu:21: The sun rises from the sea at India's southern tip.
tamil-nadu:1: Rooftops of shops around the temple
Some shops let you up to the roof for gopuram views; ask politely.
tamil-nadu:87: Silhouette the temple against the sea.
delhi:11: Perfect Mughal symmetry from the axis of the garden.
maharashtra:1: From a ferry in the harbour
The Gateway and the Taj Mahal Palace hotel together.
meghalaya:1: The stream bed below the bridge
Before the crowds, with mist in the forest.
meghalaya:28: When the sun is high, the river is clear enough to see the stones below.
gujarat:1: The salt glows white under the moon.
himachal-pradesh:117: The monastery stacked on its hill above the Spiti river.
himachal-pradesh:128: The Kinner Kailash range turns pink at dawn.
arunachal-pradesh:1: The monastery spread across the ridge in clear light.
maharashtra:95: The trail on the cliff above
See how the whole temple was carved out of the rock below you.
